stem: Sahih al-Bukhari tells that the Prophet ﷺ found Ali ibn Abi Talib asleep in the mosque, his side covered in dust, and woke him with a nickname that Ali loved best of all his names. what was it?
options: Abu Hurayrah
Abu Dharr
Abu Turab
Abu Hafs
why: In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ wiped the dust from Ali and said "get up, Abu Turab" (father of dust); the narrator adds it was the name Ali loved most. Abu Hafs is Umar's kunya; Abu Hurayrah and Abu Dharr are other companions.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Prayer (sleeping in the mosque)

es.stem: Sahih al-Bukhari cuenta que el Profeta ﷺ encontró a Ali ibn Abi Talib dormido en la mezquita, con el costado cubierto de polvo, y lo despertó con un apodo que Ali amaba más que todos sus nombres. ¿cuál era?
options: Abu Hurayrah
Abu Dharr
Abu Turab
Abu Hafs
es.why: En Sahih al-Bukhari, el Profeta ﷺ le quitó el polvo a Ali y le dijo "levántate, Abu Turab" (padre del polvo); el narrador añade que era el nombre que Ali más amaba. Abu Hafs es la kunya de Umar; Abu Hurayrah y Abu Dharr son otros compañeros.

stem: tradition holds that only one companion of the Prophet ﷺ is named in the Qur'an, in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:37). who is he?
options: Zayd ibn Harithah
Usamah ibn Zayd
Bilal ibn Rabah
Mus'ab ibn Umayr
why: Qur'an 33:37 (Pickthall): "when Zeyd had performed the necessary formality (of divorce) from her." Zayd ibn Harithah, the freed man once called Zayd ibn Muhammad, is the only companion named in the Qur'an.
source: Qur'an 33:37; Sahih al-Bukhari (Ibn Umar on "Zayd ibn Muhammad")

es.stem: la tradición sostiene que solo un compañero del Profeta ﷺ aparece con su nombre en el Corán, en la sura Al-Ahzab (33:37). ¿quién es?
options: Zayd ibn Harithah
Usamah ibn Zayd
Bilal ibn Rabah
Mus'ab ibn Umayr
es.why: Corán 33:37: "cuando Zayd hubo cumplido con ella su propósito" (la disolución del matrimonio). Zayd ibn Harithah, el liberto al que antes llamaban Zayd ibn Muhammad, es el único compañero nombrado en el Corán.

stem: in Sahih Muslim, Aisha reports that the Prophet ﷺ told his wives the one with the "longest hand" would be the first to join him after his death. what did the "longest hand" turn out to mean?
options: the arm that was longest when they measured
the wife who was the eldest among them
the wife married to him the longest
the hand that gave most in charity
why: Sahih Muslim (Book of the Merits of the Companions): the wives measured their hands, but the longest hand was Zaynab bint Jahsh's, because she worked with her hands and gave in charity; she was the first of them to die after him.
source: Sahih Muslim, Fada'il as-Sahabah (Zaynab bint Jahsh)

es.stem: en Sahih Muslim, Aisha relata que el Profeta ﷺ les dijo a sus esposas que la de la "mano más larga" sería la primera en reunirse con él después de su muerte. ¿qué resultó significar la "mano más larga"?
options: el brazo más largo cuando se midieron
la esposa de mayor edad entre ellas
la esposa casada con él por más tiempo
la mano que más daba en caridad
es.why: Sahih Muslim (Libro de los méritos de los compañeros): las esposas se midieron las manos, pero la mano más larga era la de Zaynab bint Jahsh, porque trabajaba con sus manos y daba en caridad; fue la primera de ellas en morir después de él.

stem: in Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ says of his grandson al-Hasan: "perhaps God will make peace through him between two great groups of Muslims." what event is this report linked to?
options: his win over Mu'awiyah's army in open battle
his settlement with Mu'awiyah, giving up rule
his ending of the fighting at Siffin by arbitration
his reconciling of the Aws and Khazraj tribes
why: Sahih al-Bukhari (Book of Peacemaking): al-Hasan al-Basri tells how Hasan, leading armies "like mountains," accepted terms with Mu'awiyah and stepped back from rule, sparing the bloodshed. Sunni and Shi'a Muslims read the choice differently, and both honor him. Siffin's arbitration came under Ali, and the Aws and Khazraj were reconciled at the Prophet's arrival in Medina.

es.stem: en Sahih al-Bukhari, el Profeta ﷺ dice de su nieto al-Hasan: "quizá Dios haga la paz por medio de él entre dos grandes grupos de musulmanes". ¿con qué hecho se relaciona este relato?
options: su victoria sobre el ejército de Mu'awiyah en batalla
su acuerdo con Mu'awiyah, dejando el gobierno
su fin de la lucha en Siffin mediante un arbitraje
su reconciliación de las tribus de Aws y Jazrach
es.why: Sahih al-Bukhari (Libro de la reconciliación): al-Hasan al-Basri cuenta que Hasan, al frente de ejércitos "como montañas", aceptó un acuerdo con Mu'awiyah y dejó el gobierno, evitando el derramamiento de sangre. Sunníes y chiíes leen esa decisión de modo distinto, y ambos lo honran. El arbitraje de Siffin fue en tiempos de Ali, y Aws y Jazrach se reconciliaron con la llegada del Profeta a Medina.

stem: after the Tabuk expedition, Ka'b ibn Malik admitted to the Prophet ﷺ that he had no excuse for staying behind. how, according to his own account in Sahih al-Bukhari, was his case finally settled?
options: he was forgiven that same day, like the others
he freed a slave as expiation and was pardoned
after fifty nights, a verse accepted his repentance
he rode after the army to Tabuk late and made up for it
why: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Ka'b and two others who told the truth were left without anyone speaking to them for fifty nights, until Qur'an 9:118 revealed that God had turned to "the three who were left behind." The men who gave excuses were accepted at once.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Maghazi (Ka'b ibn Malik); Qur'an 9:118

es.stem: después de la expedición de Tabuk, Ka'b ibn Malik le admitió al Profeta ﷺ que no tenía excusa por haberse quedado atrás. según su propio relato en Sahih al-Bukhari, ¿cómo se resolvió al final su caso?
options: fue perdonado ese mismo día, como los demás
liberó a un esclavo como expiación y fue perdonado
tras cincuenta noches, un verso aceptó su arrepentimiento
salió tarde tras el ejército hacia Tabuk y así lo compensó
es.why: En Sahih al-Bukhari, Ka'b y otros dos que dijeron la verdad pasaron cincuenta noches sin que nadie les hablara, hasta que Corán 9:118 reveló que Dios se había vuelto hacia "los tres que se quedaron atrás". A los que dieron excusas se les aceptó de inmediato.

stem: plague breaks out in the city where a merchant lives, and he wants to flee to a healthy town. by the hadith Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf quoted to Umar on the road to Syria (Sahih al-Bukhari), what should he do?
options: stay where he is and not flee the land
leave quickly, from God's decree to God's decree
leave, as long as he goes to a land without it
go wherever he likes, since all is already decreed
why: Sahih al-Bukhari: "if you hear of it in a land, do not enter it; and if it breaks out in a land where you are, do not leave it to flee from it." Umar's words about running from God's decree to God's decree were about not entering, not about leaving a plague land.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab at-Tibb (Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf)

es.stem: estalla la peste en la ciudad donde vive un comerciante, y él quiere huir a un pueblo sano. según el hadiz que Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf le citó a Umar en el camino a Siria (Sahih al-Bukhari), ¿qué debe hacer?
options: quedarse donde está y no huir de esa tierra
irse rápido, del decreto de Dios al decreto de Dios
irse, siempre que vaya a una tierra sin peste
ir adonde quiera, pues todo ya está decretado
es.why: Sahih al-Bukhari: "si oyen de ella en una tierra, no entren en ella; y si estalla en una tierra donde ustedes están, no salgan de ella para huir". Las palabras de Umar sobre huir del decreto de Dios al decreto de Dios se referían a no entrar, no a salir de una tierra con peste.

stem: In hadith scholarship, as defined by Ibn Hajar among others, who counts as a sahabi, a companion of the Prophet ﷺ?
why: Ibn Hajar (al-Isabah) defines a companion as one who met the Prophet ﷺ believing in him and died as a believer. Meeting, not seeing, is the test, so a blind man counts, and the length of time together does not matter.
source: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, al-Isabah fi Tamyiz as-Sahabah (introduction)

rubric.point: Says the person met the Prophet ﷺ (was in his presence) in his lifetime. Saying only 'lived at the same time as him' does not count.
Says the person believed in him at that meeting and died as a believer (a Muslim). Mentioning only belief at the meeting, or only dying Muslim, counts as partly.
Adds that meeting, not seeing, is what counts (so a blind man qualifies), or that one meeting is enough however short (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En el estudio del hadiz, según la definición de Ibn Hajar entre otros, ¿quién cuenta como sahabi, un compañero del Profeta ﷺ?
es.why: Ibn Hajar (al-Isabah) define al compañero como quien se encontró con el Profeta ﷺ creyendo en él y murió como creyente. La prueba es el encuentro, no la vista, así que un ciego cuenta, y no importa cuánto tiempo estuvieron juntos.

stem: In the speech the sirah of Ibn Ishaq (as passed on by Ibn Hisham) gives Abu Bakr when he first addressed the people after receiving their pledge in Medina, what did he ask of them?
why: Ibn Ishaq / Ibn Hisham: "I have been given authority over you, and I am not the best of you. If I do well, help me; if I do wrong, set me right... Obey me as long as I obey God and His Messenger; if I disobey them, you owe me no obedience."
source: Ibn Hisham, as-Sirah an-Nabawiyyah (Ibn Ishaq), the pledge at the Saqifah

rubric.point: Says he asked them to correct or set him right if he did wrong (and help him if he did well). 'He asked for their support' alone counts as partly.
Says their obedience was conditional: obey him only as long as he obeys God and His Messenger. 'Obey me' without the condition does not count.
Mentions that he said he was not the best of them, or that the weak would be strong in his eyes until he secured their right, or that truthfulness is a trust (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En el discurso que la sira de Ibn Ishaq (transmitida por Ibn Hisham) atribuye a Abu Bakr cuando habló por primera vez a la gente tras recibir su juramento en Medina, ¿qué les pidió?
es.why: Ibn Ishaq / Ibn Hisham: "Se me ha dado autoridad sobre ustedes, y no soy el mejor de ustedes. Si obro bien, ayúdenme; si obro mal, corríjanme... Obedézcanme mientras yo obedezca a Dios y a Su Mensajero; si los desobedezco, no me deben obediencia".
